name: Joshua Rotenberg
body: I'm applying for the Growth Marketing Manager role. The phrase in your posting I'd point at is repeatable, scalable systems, because that's the distinction I care about too. At Solenzo I built an acquisition and lifecycle system of 20+ workflows covering capture, routing, qualification, booking with confirmations and reminders, no-show recovery, onboarding nurture, and long-term reactivation, plus segmented outreach engines and an automated audit workflow that scored a company's digital footprint and enrolled 180+ contacts. That's a system that keeps running, not a campaign that ends.

On the analytics side, at Level Agency I built the reporting frameworks that tracked ROI, CAC, LTV, and conversion KPIs, and used them to make optimization and budget recommendations. I build the dashboards myself rather than requesting them, which matters when the question is where the next dollar should go. And I'm comfortable working the seam with Product and Engineering: at Birdeye I routed structured customer feedback into roadmap decisions, and at Solenzo the most useful thing I did on one paid account was follow a conversion gap past the ad platform into the on-site experience, where the actual problem was.

On referral and partner acquisition, I ran a 15 to 20 partner reseller and referral network at Birdeye, recruiting and onboarding them, building the training and communication sequences that made them productive, and retaining all but one.

I'll be direct about scope. My growth work has been B2B and service-business rather than consumer membership, so the specific rhythms of subscription acquisition would be new context for me, though CAC discipline, funnel analysis, and conversion testing are not. I'd welcome the conversation.
